checklist.1_sourced_stat_first_50_words: PASS — '62% of startups now have more than half their codebase written by AI (Supabase State of Startups, 2026)' appears in opening sentence.
checklist.2_builder_stack_first_person: FAIL — n8n, Claude API, Supabase, MCP are all mentioned throughout, but not anchored to Payal's own builds. Article is written in advisory/second-person voice ('when you implement typed handoff contracts...'). The What I Would Do section uses 'If I were setting up this stack' (hypothetical), not 'I have shipped this stack.' Compared to portfolio Article 1 ('The pipeline described here is live and in production') and Article 2 ('This is the story of a German language exam preparation app built from zero'), this article lacks the first-person build anchor that establishes builder authority vs. analyst commentary.

checklist.10_no_buzzwords_numerals: PASS — No buzzwords found. Numbers in numerals throughout (62%, $100/month, 9,400+, 2,063, 4 hours, 30 minutes, 5x). Sentence case throughout.
checklist.11_all_claims_sourced: PASS — All 5 factual claims have named source + date: Supabase State of Startups 2026, MindStudio 2026, agence-scroll.com June 2026, n8n documentation 2026, SaaStr 2026.
checklist.12_voice_authenticity: PASS — Opening paragraphs are direct, data-first, punchy. 'Not as a prototype layer. As the production system.' is authentic to Payal's established voice pattern. No preamble.
checklist.13_sources_match_meta: PASS — All 5 sources in meta.json sources array match the 5 inline citations in article body exactly.
checklist.14_linkedin_native_value: PASS — 'Most are choosing tools randomly — and rebuilding their stack every 3 months.' is a LinkedIn-native insight not present in the article body.
checklist.15_no_undefined_acronyms: FAIL — MCP appears in the title and throughout the body but is never expanded to 'Model Context Protocol.' A cold reader unfamiliar with MCP would need to infer from context ('MCP owns integration — how Claude reads and writes to live systems in real time'). The acronym is described but not spelled out. All other acronyms: RLS is expanded ('Row-Level Security'), DORA is cited with EU regulation number (EU 2022/2554), GDPR is widely known. Only MCP is undefined.
